records.summary: FERC's December 29, 2025 final order (Docket P-10856-141, 193 FERC ¶61,242) TERMINATED the Au Train Hydroelectric Project license by implied surrender, effective that day's close of business, with existing facilities LEFT IN PLACE. In 2025 foreclosure, Stephenson Bank acquired 18/22 project parcels and later sold those 18 to D. Charles Trust Investments, LLC (including powerhouse and surrounding project buffer), but individual tourist parking and falls-side parcel title/right of way are not mapped by this order. Michigan EGLE now holds state dam-safety jurisdiction; termination neither orders immediate dam removal nor establishes all waterfall visitor routes closed or open. Munising tourism describes two separate upper/lower falls visitor stops near utility gates, but that older guidance does not establish October 2026 parking, public gate entry, walkway, flow conditions or new property owner consent.
records.guidance: Do not treat either of the old Power Dam Road upper/lower tourism lots as current authorized parking; do not pass power plant or dam gates without posted public authorization. records.reviewLimitations: Original 2025 report about a proposed license surrender is superseded by FERC's December 29 FINAL termination order. The FERC order ends federal licensing, not every existing owner property right or recreational activity. Ownership changes within project boundary do not map the exact upper/lower parking parcels.
records.nextEvidence: Current 2026 rights owner/EGLE source explicitly documenting a lawful publicly accessible upper and/or lower falls visitor parking area and foot corridor on utility land; verify separate two-view routes, gate policy, dam safety/flow notices and legal parking. records.summary: State GIS #48 'Narrow Falls' at 46.562534,-90.081582 is approximately 63m from independent 'Narrows Falls' point 46.56304,-90.08122. Field survey calls it a submerged-rock ripple of around 3 inches, while generalized tourism lists repeatedly ascribe a 10-foot waterfall/steep scramble to a point around 46.6264,-90.0483, about 7.5km farther north. These cannot be treated as identical visitor destinations.
